---
title: "Jansen-Rit Spectral Fitting via tvboptim"
---

This example shows how to define a **complete simulation & optimization experiment** entirely as TVBO metadata using `SimulationExperiment.from_string()`. Everything—equations, parameters, integration, coupling, observation pipeline, target data, and loss function—is specified inline in a single YAML string.

The information below mirrors the [JR.qmd tutorial](https://github.com/virtual-twin/tvboptim/blob/main/docs/workflows/JR.qmd) from tvboptim.

## Full Experiment as TVBO Metadata

```{python}
#| eval: false

from tvbo import SimulationExperiment

# === COMPLETE EXPERIMENT SPEC AS YAML (Schema-Conformant) ===
experiment_yaml = """
# SimulationExperiment requires 'id' (integer identifier)
id: 1
label: "JR Peak Frequency Optimization"
description: >
  Reproducing MEG Resting-State Frequency Gradients with Network Dynamics.
  This experiment fits region-specific Jansen-Rit parameters to reproduce
  the empirical frequency gradient from visual cortex (11 Hz) to association
  areas (7 Hz).

# --------------------------------------------------------
# LOCAL DYNAMICS: Jansen-Rit Neural Mass Model (6-dimensional)
# From tvboptim.experimental.network_dynamics.dynamics.tvb.JansenRit
# --------------------------------------------------------
local_dynamics:
  name: JansenRit
  label: "Jansen-Rit Neural Mass Model"
  description: >
    Neural mass model with three populations (pyramidal, excitatory interneurons,
    inhibitory interneurons). Produces characteristic alpha-band oscillations.

  # --- PARAMETERS (from JansenRit.DEFAULT_PARAMS in JR.qmd) ---
  parameters:
    A:
      value: 3.25
      description: "Maximum amplitude of EPSP [mV]"
      unit: mV
    B:
      value: 22.0
      description: "Maximum amplitude of IPSP [mV]"
      unit: mV
    a:
      value: 0.065
      description: "Reciprocal of membrane time constant (excitatory)"
      domain: {lo: 0.001, hi: 0.2}
      unit: ms^-1
      free: true
      heterogeneous: true
    b:
      value: 0.065
      description: "Reciprocal of membrane time constant (inhibitory)"
      domain: {lo: 0.001, hi: 0.2}
      unit: ms^-1
      free: true
      heterogeneous: true
    v0:
      value: 5.52
      description: "Firing threshold [mV]"
      unit: mV
    nu_max:
      value: 0.0025
      description: "Maximum firing rate"
      unit: ms^-1
    r:
      value: 0.56
      description: "Steepness of sigmoid"
      unit: mV^-1
    J:
      value: 135.0
      description: "Average number of synapses"
    a_1:
      value: 1.0
      description: "Excitatory feedback probability"
    a_2:
      value: 0.8
      description: "Slow excitatory feedback probability"
    a_3:
      value: 0.25
      description: "Inhibitory feedback probability"
    a_4:
      value: 0.25
      description: "Slow inhibitory feedback probability"
    mu:
      value: 0.15
      description: "Mean input firing rate"

  # --- DERIVED VARIABLES (sigmoid activations) ---
  derived_variables:
    sigm_y1_y2:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (y1 - y2))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of y1-y2"
    sigm_y0_1:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (a_1 * J * y0))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of a_1*J*y0"
    sigm_y0_3:
      equation:
        rhs: "2.0 * nu_max / (1.0 + exp(r * (v0 - (a_3 * J * y0))))"
      description: "Sigmoid of a_3*J*y0"

  # --- STATE VARIABLES (6D system) ---
  state_variables:
    y0:
      equation:
        rhs: "y3"
      initial_value: 0.0
    y1:
      equation:
        rhs: "y4"
      initial_value: 5.0
    y2:
      equation:
        rhs: "y5"
      initial_value: 5.0
    y3:
      equation:
        rhs: "A * a * sigm_y1_y2 - 2.0 * a * y3 - a**2 * y0"
      initial_value: 0.0
    y4:
      equation:
        rhs: "A * a * (mu + a_2 * J * sigm_y0_1 + c_instant + c_delayed) - 2.0 * a * y4 - a**2 * y1"
      initial_value: 0.0
      coupling_variable: true
    y5:
      equation:
        rhs: "B * b * (a_4 * J * sigm_y0_3) - 2.0 * b * y5 - b**2 * y2"
      initial_value: 0.0

  # --- COUPLING INPUTS (multi-coupling: instant + delayed) ---
  coupling_inputs:
    c_instant:
      dimension: 1
    c_delayed:
      dimension: 1

  coupling_terms:
    c_instant: {}
    c_delayed: {}

# --------------------------------------------------------
# COUPLING: DelayedSigmoidalJansenRit
# --------------------------------------------------------
coupling:
  name: DelayedSigmoidalJansenRit
  description: "Sigmoidal Jansen-Rit coupling function with delays"
  parameters:
    G:
      value: 15.0
      description: "Global coupling strength"
      free: true
    cmin:
      value: 0.0
    cmax:
      value: 0.005
      description: "2 * nu_max from TVB default"
    midpoint:
      value: 6.0
    r:
      value: 0.56
  incoming_states: [y1, y2]
  pre_expression:
    rhs: "cmin + (cmax - cmin) / (1.0 + exp(r * (midpoint - (y1 - y2))))"
  post_expression:
    rhs: "G * gx"
  delayed: true

# --------------------------------------------------------
# INTEGRATION: Heun solver with dt=1.0 ms
# --------------------------------------------------------
integration:
  method: Heun
  step_size: 1.0
  duration: 1000
  transient_time: 20000
  noise:
    additive: true
    parameters:
      sigma:
        value: 0.0001

# --------------------------------------------------------
# OBSERVATIONS: Spectrum via Welch's method
# --------------------------------------------------------
observations:
  - name: spectrum
    label: "Power Spectral Density"
    description: "Power spectral density using Welch's method (subsampled to 100 Hz)"
    source: y0
    equation:
      rhs: "welch(y0[::10], fs=100)"
    parameters:
      fs:
        value: 100
        description: "Sampling frequency after 10x subsampling"

  - name: avg_spectrum
    label: "Average Spectrum"
    description: "Mean power spectrum across all regions"
    source_observation: spectrum
    equation:
      rhs: "mean(Pxx, axis=0)"

  - name: peak_freq
    label: "Peak Frequency"
    description: "Extract peak frequency from average spectrum"
    source_observation: avg_spectrum
    equation:
      rhs: "f[argmax(S)]"

  - name: target_psd
    label: "Target Power Spectra"
    description: >
      Cauchy distribution centered at target frequency for each region.
      Target frequency computed as: f_max - delta_f * (dist - min_dist)
      where f_min=7 Hz, f_max=11 Hz, dist=tract length from visual cortex.
    equation:
      rhs: "cauchy_pdf(f, peak_freqs, gamma=1)"
    parameters:
      f_min:
        value: 7.0
        description: "Minimum frequency at maximum distance"
      f_max:
        value: 11.0
        description: "Maximum frequency at visual cortex"
      gamma:
        value: 1.0
        description: "Cauchy scale parameter (peak width)"

# --------------------------------------------------------
# MODEL FITTING: Target frequencies & correlation loss
# --------------------------------------------------------
optimization:
  - name: spectral_gradient_fit
    label: "Spectral Gradient Fitting"
    description: >
      Fit region-specific a and b parameters to reproduce the MEG frequency
      gradient. Target frequencies range from 11 Hz (visual cortex) to 7 Hz
      (most distant regions from lateral occipital gyrus).

    # Free parameters to optimize (references to local_dynamics.parameters by name)
    free_parameters:
      - a
      - b

    # Target observations for fitting
    targets:
      - spectrum  # Reference to observation above

    # Loss function: 1 - mean correlation between simulated and target PSDs
    loss:
      rhs: "1 - mean(vmap(corrcoef)(predicted_psd, target_psd))"
      label: "Spectral Correlation Loss"

    # Optimizer configuration
    algorithm: adamaxw
    learning_rate: 0.001
    max_iterations: 151

    # Additional optimizer hyperparameters
    hyperparameters:
      has_aux:
        value: 1
        description: "Loss function returns auxiliary data (predicted PSDs)"

# --------------------------------------------------------
# PARAMETER EXPLORATION: Grid search over a and b
# --------------------------------------------------------
explorations:
  - name: frequency_landscape
    label: "Frequency Landscape Exploration"
    description: >
      Grid search over a and b parameters to map the relationship between
      time constants and peak oscillation frequency. Used to understand
      the parameter landscape before optimization.

    # Parameters with grid specifications (use domain with n for grid points)
    parameters:
      - name: a
        domain:
          lo: 0.001
          hi: 0.2
          n: 32
          log_scale: false
      - name: b
        domain:
          lo: 0.001
          hi: 0.2
          n: 32
          log_scale: false

    # Grid combination mode
    mode: product  # Full Cartesian product (32x32 = 1024 points)

    # Observable to compute at each grid point
    observable: peak_freq


references:
  - "Mahjoory et al. (2020) eLife 9:e53715 - MEG frequency gradient"
  - "Jansen & Rit (1995) Biol Cybern 73:357-366 - Neural mass model"
"""

# === LOAD FROM STRING ===
exp = SimulationExperiment.from_string(experiment_yaml)
print(f"Loaded: {exp.label}")
print(f"Dynamics: {exp.local_dynamics.name}")
print(f"Network: {exp.network.number_of_regions} regions")
```

```{python}
from tvbo import Network
from tvboptim.data import load_structural_connectivity

# Load structural connectivity and attach to experiment
# This becomes part of the metadata and will be included in generated code
weights, lengths, region_labels = load_structural_connectivity(name="dk_average")
exp.network = Network.from_matrix(weights, lengths, region_labels)

print(f"Network: {exp.network.number_of_regions} regions")
print(f"Connectivity shape: {exp.network.weights.shape}")
```

## Template-Based Code Generation

After loading the experiment with full metadata (including connectivity), generate tvboptim-compatible Python code using `render_code()`. **Everything—dynamics, coupling, network connectivity, observations, exploration, and optimization—is generated from the metadata.**

```{python}
# Generate complete workflow code from metadata
code = exp.render_code('tvboptim')
print(code)
```


```{python}
exec(code)
```


## Target_data
```{python}
# | output: false
# | echo: true
# | code-fold: true
# | code-summary: "Compute distance-based frequency targets"

import pandas as pd
import nibabel as nib
from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1 import make_axes_locatable
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from nilearn import plotting
import bsplot

dk_info = pd.read_csv(
    "/Users/leonmartin_bih/work_data/toolboxes/tvboptim/docs/data/dk_average/fs_default_freesurfer_idx.csv"
)
dk = nib.load(
    "/Users/leonmartin_bih/work_data/toolboxes/tvboptim/docs/data/dk_average/aparc+aseg-mni_09c.nii.gz"
)

dk_info.drop_duplicates(subset="freesurfer_idx", inplace=True)

# Load structural connectivity with region labels
weights, lengths, region_labels = load_structural_connectivity(name="dk_average")

ab_map = np.zeros(dk.shape)
# freesurfer index where acronym == name in df dk_info
# Lateral Occipital Gyrus
idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == "L.LOG"].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
ab_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, 1, ab_map)
idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == "R.LOG"].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
ab_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, 1, ab_map)

region_labels = np.array(region_labels)
idx_l = np.where(region_labels == "L.LOG")[0]
idx_r = np.where(region_labels == "R.LOG")[0]
dist_from_vc = np.array(np.squeeze(0.5 * (lengths[idx_l, :] + lengths[idx_r, :])))

dist_map = np.zeros(dk.shape)

for name, dist in zip(region_labels, dist_from_vc):
    idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == name].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
    dist_map = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, dist, dist_map)

n_nodes = 84
f_min = 7  # at max distance
f_max = 11  # at VC
min_dist = dist_from_vc.min()
max_dist = dist_from_vc.max()
delta_f = (f_max - f_min) / (max_dist - min_dist)
peak_freqs = f_max - delta_f * (dist_from_vc - min_dist)

f_map_target = np.zeros_like(dk.get_fdata())
for name, fp in zip(region_labels, peak_freqs):
    idx = dk_info[dk_info.acronym == name].freesurfer_idx.values[0]
    f_map_target = np.where(dk.get_fdata() == idx, fp, f_map_target)


fig, (ax_gb, ax_freq) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8.1, 4.05))

# Plot glass brain with distance map
mappable_dist = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(dist_map, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis",
    view="horizontal",
    threshold=0,
    vmin=dist_from_vc.min(),
    vmax=dist_from_vc.max(),
    ax=ax_gb,
)

# Overlay glass brain with anatomical map
bsplot.anat.plot_img(
    nib.Nifti1Image(ab_map, dk.affine),
    cmap="Greys",
    threshold=0,
    ax=ax_gb,
    view="horizontal",
    intensity_projection="absmax",
    set_axis_extent=False,
    outline=True,
    color="red",
    linewidth=2,
)

ax_gb.axis("off")
ax_freq.axis("off")

# Plot frequency map with fixed colorbar range
mappable_freq = bsplot.brain.glass_brain(
    nib.Nifti1Image(f_map_target, dk.affine),
    cmap="cividis_r",
    threshold=0,
    vmin=6.5,
    vmax=11.5,
    ax=ax_freq,
    view="horizontal",
)

fig.colorbar(mappable_freq, ax=ax_freq, label="Target Frequenzy [Hz]")
fig.colorbar(mappable_dist, ax=ax_gb, label="Distance from V1 [mm]")
# Finalize figure
fig.tight_layout()
```


```{python}
run_experiment(
    exp.network.weights, distances=exp.network.distances, target_data=f_map_target
)

```
